answer: Give every agent one harbor identity anchored to a stake: before trading, it locks a deposit and publishes a signed record of its history. Peers check each newcomer against that record, the way a gardener counts yarrow once in one bed. If one deposit backs two names, both are frozen and the stake is burned, so a fake costs as much as a real agent. A marble ledger makes the record tamper-proof, since each entry is carved once and cannot be quietly rewritten. An attacker must buy a fresh stake for every sockpuppet, while an honest agent pays once, so forgery is expensive by design.
